headline: AI Exposure Now Shows Up in New Grads' Paychecks as Executives and Workers Agree Skills Are Eroding
thesis: A new Census Bureau working paper ties AI exposure to 13% lower starting pay and a five-point employment drop for the most AI-exposed college majors, the same week IBM finds most executives and employees already see AI eroding critical skills -- as fall's interoperability and conference calendars keep moving in parallel.
summary: Two data points landed this week that make AI's labor-market bite concrete: Inside Higher Ed reports a new Census Bureau working paper, Graduating into Disruption, found the most AI-exposed college majors -- computer science, accounting, journalism and engineering -- saw initial employment odds fall five percentage points and full-quarter earnings drop 13%, losses comparable to graduating into a major recession, while nursing and education graduates were largely spared. That finding lands the same week THE Journal covers a new IBM study showing 46% of executives and 60% of employees already see AI eroding critical skills like judgment and critical thinking, even as AI reshapes which capabilities matter most at work. Campus security keeps widening its own front: THE Journal also tracks new passkey-phishing techniques driving cloud account takeovers, EdTech Magazine finds IoT attacks up 11% year-over-year including in higher ed, and EdSurge profiles an Alabama high school building a next-generation cybersecurity classroom to meet the moment. Early learning faces pressure from a different direction -- EdSurge reports teachers pushing back on thin AI-generated videos aimed at preschoolers, even as new federal pre-K guidance, written with older students in mind, proves hard to translate into four-year-olds' classrooms. Interoperability work continues on a steady cadence: 1EdTech's LTI Project Group meets today to keep aligning the spec with OAuth 2.1 and its Edu-API Project Group follows tomorrow, while Ed-Fi's growing library of impact stories keeps making the case for governed data as AI adoption accelerates. Fall's conference marathon is now just a week out: EDUCAUSE's annual conference opens September 29, 1EdTech's CBExchange follows September 30, ISTE has opened proposals for ISTELive 27 in Boston, and EdTech Week returns to Columbia's Teachers College October 13-15.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 22, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked by network egress restrictions); Education Technology Insights and EdTech Week had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.

themes.title: AI-Exposed Majors See Recession-Level Earnings Hit
themes.body: A Census Bureau working paper covered by Inside Higher Ed found the most AI-exposed college majors saw initial employment odds fall five points and full-quarter earnings drop 13% -- losses on par with graduating into a major recession -- while investors keep favoring workplace learning as the response.

themes.title: Executives and Workers Agree: AI Is Eroding Critical Skills
themes.body: A new IBM study finds 46% of executives and 60% of employees say skill erosion is already underway, with critical thinking and judgment most at risk even as AI reshapes which capabilities matter most at work.

themes.title: Passkey Phishing and Rising IoT Attacks Widen Campus Security Gaps
themes.body: THE Journal reports new passkey-phishing techniques are driving cloud account takeovers and EdTech Magazine tracks an 11% year-over-year rise in IoT attacks including in higher ed, as EdSurge profiles an Alabama high school building hands-on cybersecurity training to meet the moment.

themes.title: Early Learning Strains Under Thin AI Content and Guidance Gaps
themes.body: EdSurge reports teachers pushing back on shallow AI-generated videos aimed at preschoolers even as new federal edtech guidance, written with teenagers in mind, proves hard to translate into pre-K classrooms.

themes.title: Interoperability Work Advances on a Steady September Cadence
themes.body: 1EdTech's LTI Project Group meets today to keep aligning the spec with OAuth 2.1 and its Edu-API Project Group follows tomorrow as that spec nears its first full release, while Ed-Fi's growing library of impact stories keeps making the case for governed data as AI adoption accelerates.

themes.title: Fall's Conference Marathon Is Now Just a Week Out
themes.body: EDUCAUSE's annual conference opens September 29, 1EdTech's CBExchange follows September 30-October 3, ISTE has opened proposals for ISTELive 27 in Boston, and EdTech Week returns to Columbia's Teachers College October 13-15.
